text:
Predicates:
PerformsOften(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
Attends(x) ::: x attends school events.
Engaged(x) ::: x is very engaged with school events.
Inactive(x) ::: x is inactive and disinterested member of community.
Chaperones(x, y) ::: x chaperones y.
HighSchoolDance(y) ::: y is a high school dance.
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
YoungerOrTeen(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.
WishesFurther(x) ::: x wishes to further academic and educational opportunities.

Premises:
∀x (PerformsOften(x) → Attends(x) ∧ Engaged(x)) ::: If people perform often, then they attend and are engaged.
∀x (PerformsOften(x) ∨ (Inactive(x) ∧ ¬Engaged(x))) ::: People either perform often or are inactive and disinterested.
∀x ∀y (Chaperones(x, y) ∧ HighSchoolDance(y) → ¬Student(x)) ::: If someone chaperones a dance, then they are not a student.
∀x (Inactive(x) ∧ Disinterested(x) → Chaperones(x, y) ∧ HighSchoolDance(y)) ::: All inactive and disinterested members chaperone dances.
∀x (YoungerOrTeen(x) ∧ WishesFurther(x) → Student(x)) ::: Young children and teenagers who wish to further their education are students.
BonnieEither ::: (Attends(Bonnie) ∧ Engaged(Bonnie) ∧ Student(Bonnie)) ∨ (¬Attends(Bonnie) ∧ ¬Engaged(Bonnie) ∧ ¬Student(Bonnie)) ::: Bonnie either attends and is engaged, and is a student, or neither.

Conclusion:
(Chaperones(Bonnie, y) ∨ ¬Chaperones(Bonnie, y)) → (WishesFurther(Bonnie) ∧ YoungerOrTeen(Bonnie) ∧ Inactive(Bonnie)) ::: If Bonnie either chaperones dances or not, then she is both a young child or teenager who wishes to further her education and an inactive, disinterested member of the community.
